title: Kafka on the Shore
author: Haruki Murakami
notes: Two stories that never quite meet and still feel like one. I stopped trying to solve it halfway through and enjoyed it far more.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
notes: Quiet enough that the horror arrives late, and it stays. The calmest sad book I've read.

title: Let the Great World Spin
author: Colum McCann
notes: A whole city strung on one wire walk. Every chapter changes voice and somehow it holds.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
notes: Funnier than I remembered from school. Mr Collins alone is worth the reread.
favoriteLine: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
notes: Shorter than its reputation. The last page does all the work.
favoriteLine: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.

title: Stoner
author: John Williams
notes: An ordinary life told with total attention. I didn't expect a book about a farm boy turned professor to wreck me.

title: The Remains of the Day
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
notes: Halfway. Stevens is the most unreliable reliable narrator.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
notes: Read it on a foggy week, which felt like cheating.
favoriteLine: Mr. Holmes, they were the footprints of a gigantic hound!

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
notes: The midpoint turn is earned. I disliked everyone and kept reading anyway.

title: The Secret History
author: Donna Tartt
notes: Tells you the murder on page one and is still unbearably tense.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
notes: The template for a hundred books since, and still the tightest.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
notes: A fast read with one big trick. Fun once.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
notes: Less about surveillance than about language. Newspeak is the scariest part.

title: Blindsight
author: Peter Watts
notes: Hard going and full of ideas about consciousness I'm still chewing on.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
notes: Ecology, religion and politics as one system. The appendices are worth reading.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
notes: The ice crossing is one of the great friendships in fiction.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
notes: Pure problem-solving joy. Rocky deserves his own book.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
notes: Short, strange, and more political than I expected.
favoriteLine: It is a law of nature we overlook, that intellectual versatility is the compensation for change, danger, and trouble.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
notes: The creature is the most eloquent person in it.
favoriteLine: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
notes: Comfort reading. The riddle game is perfect.

title: A Wizard of Earthsea
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
notes: A whole magic system built on true names, in under two hundred pages.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
notes: Still in the halls. Not sure what's going on, happy not to know yet.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
notes: Gorgeous sentences, and I'm still waiting for book three like everyone else.

title: Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell
author: Susanna Clarke
notes: Footnotes that are better than most novels.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
notes: Big claims, fast pace. Good for starting arguments at dinner.

title: Bad Blood
author: John Carreyrou
notes: Reads like a thriller. The whistleblowers are the heroes.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
notes: About memory as much as school. Hard to read and hard to put down.

title: The Guns of August
author: Barbara W. Tuchman
notes: Thirty days that decided the century, told hour by hour.

title: Shoe Dog
author: Phil Knight
notes: Much more anxious and honest than a founder memoir has to be.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
notes: Long, and it doesn't flatter him, which I liked.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
notes: Understood about seventy percent. The light-cone chapter finally clicked.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
notes: Changed how I see almost every animal documentary.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
notes: Slow in the middle, then the last chapter lands it.
favoriteLine: There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one.

title: The Gene
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
notes: On the Mendel chapters. Part history, part family memoir.

title: Being Wrong
author: Kathryn Schulz
notes: Makes a strong case that being wrong feels exactly like being right.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
notes: Dense, but System 1 versus System 2 is now how I think about thinking.

title: 101 Essays That Will Change The Way You Think
author: Brianna Wiest
notes: Best read a few essays at a time, not front to back.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: A private notebook that became everyone's. I keep it on the desk.
favoriteLine: Remember this, that very little is needed to make a happy life.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
notes: One idea, explained well and often. The two-minute rule stuck.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
notes: Short, and it puts every complaint in perspective.

title: The Courage to Be Disliked
author: Ichiro Kishimi
notes: A dialogue that argues with you. I didn't agree with all of it, which was the point.
